title: One Kinase, Many Targets—and Its Brakes

scenes.visual: Reopen the exact cell-edge cross-section and colour map from the first film, marked 'schematic': warm amber (#F59E0B) insulin and receptor, soft teal (#2DD4BF) IRS-1, sky blue (#38BDF8) PI 3-kinase, slate (#64748B) PIP2, bright gold (#FACC15) PIP3, bright coral-red (#F43F5E) active Akt with two yellow-white 'P' badges. Add mint-green (#34D399) for PTEN/erasers, dusty indigo (#818CF8) for resting inhibitory targets (dimming to grey when switched off), and emerald (#10B981) for GLUT4, glucose, and glycogen. Title appears: One Kinase, Many Targets—and Its Brakes.

scenes.tts: The first film showed P I P three recruiting Akt to the membrane, where two phosphates activate it. Once Akt turns on, how does one kinase drive different tissue jobs without running forever? The answer combines tissue-specific targets with lipid erasers and negative feedback.

scenes.visual: Active coral-red Akt pulses on the gold PIP3 patch at the top of the frame. Three gentle arrows fan downward into three dimly lit zones below—labelled 'Muscle & fat', 'Glycogen', and 'Liver nucleus'—while a mint-green PTEN block waits beside the membrane.

scenes.tts: Start in muscle and fat cells. At rest, emerald glucose transporters wait inside small vesicles. A brake protein, A S one sixty, holds those vesicles back. Active Akt phosphorylates that brake and switches it off. With help from other proteins, vesicles then fuse with the surface, letting glucose stream in.
scenes.caption: Start in muscle and fat cells. At rest, emerald glucose transporters wait inside small vesicles. A brake protein, AS160, holds those vesicles back. Active Akt phosphorylates that brake and switches it off. With help from other proteins, vesicles then fuse with the surface, letting glucose stream in.
scenes.visual: Focus on the 'Muscle & fat' zone (schematic). Emerald GLUT4 channels sit in round intracellular vesicles tethered by an indigo block labelled 'AS160 (Rab GAP)'. Coral-red Akt stamps a yellow-white 'P' onto AS160, which turns grey and releases. Vesicles glide upward and fuse into the bilayer, inserting emerald GLUT4 doors through which emerald glucose dots flow inside.

scenes.tts: Next, watch glycogen storage inside muscle and liver. An enzyme called G S K three normally phosphorylates glycogen synthase and keeps it slow. Active Akt phosphorylates G S K three and shuts it down. With that brake gone, glycogen synthase speeds up and builds storage chains.
scenes.caption: Next, watch glycogen storage inside muscle and liver. An enzyme called GSK3 normally phosphorylates glycogen synthase and keeps it slow. Active Akt phosphorylates GSK3 and shuts it down. With that brake gone, glycogen synthase speeds up and builds storage chains.
scenes.visual: Shift smoothly to the 'Glycogen' zone of the same cell. Indigo GSK3 holds an emerald glycogen synthase block stalled with red inhibitory marks. Coral-red Akt stamps 'P' on GSK3; GSK3 dims grey and drifts away. Inhibitory marks vanish from glycogen synthase, which spins into action linking emerald glucose beads into a branched glycogen chain.
scenes.narration: Next, watch glycogen storage inside muscle and liver. An enzyme called GSK3 normally phosphorylates glycogen synthase and keeps it slow. Active Akt phosphorylates GSK3 and shuts it down. With that brake gone, glycogen synthase speeds up and builds storage chains.

scenes.tts: Now zoom into a liver nucleus. Between meals, fox oh one sits on D N A, driving genes that build new glucose. Active Akt phosphorylates fox oh one. Partner proteins then help move it out and hold it in the cytosol. Over hours, those glucose-making genes quiet down.
scenes.caption: Now zoom into a liver nucleus. Between meals, FOXO1 sits on DNA, driving genes that build new glucose. Active Akt phosphorylates FOXO1. Partner proteins then help move it out and hold it in the cytosol. Over hours, those glucose-making genes quiet down.
scenes.visual: Pan down to a rounded liver nucleus. Indigo FOXO1 sits on a DNA ribbon with glowing transcription arrows labelled 'Gluconeogenic genes'. Coral-red Akt enters briefly and stamps 'P' onto FOXO1; small anchor blocks labelled '14-3-3' clasp phosphorylated FOXO1 and accompany it out through a nuclear pore and hold it in the cytosol. The DNA transcription arrows fade dim.
scenes.narration: Now zoom into a liver nucleus. Between meals, FOXO1 sits on DNA, driving genes that build new glucose. Active Akt phosphorylates FOXO1. Partner proteins then help move it out and hold it in the cytosol. Over hours, those glucose-making genes quiet down.

scenes.tts: Notice the shared pattern across all three jobs. Akt switches each target protein off. Removing a brake turns uptake and storage up; removing a driver turns glucose-making genes down. Keep this second rule. Akt phosphorylates tissue-specific targets, while erasers and feedback limit the signal.

scenes.visual: Brief three-column schematic summary banner across the cytosol showing the three greyed-out indigo targets with 'P' badges: 'AS160 off -> GLUT4 up', 'GSK3 off -> glycogen up', 'FOXO1 out -> liver genes down', then pull smoothly back up to the plasma membrane. Empathy fix: Show 'Brake off (AS160, GSK3) → uptake, storage up' and 'Driver off (FOXO1) → glucose-making genes down' as spoken.

scenes.tts: Every signal needs an off switch. Tyrosine phosphatases reset the receptor and docking protein. Mint-green P ten strips the three-phosphate from P I P three, restoring slate P I P two. With its address gone, Akt leaves and loses both phosphates. Downstream kinases also mark I R S one on serines, making it a poorer landing pad for P I three kinase.
scenes.caption: Every signal needs an off switch. Tyrosine phosphatases reset the receptor and docking protein. Mint-green PTEN strips the 3-phosphate from PIP3, restoring slate PIP2. With its address gone, Akt leaves and loses both phosphates. Downstream kinases also mark IRS-1 on serines, making it a poorer landing pad for PI 3-kinase.
scenes.visual: Back at the membrane cross-section. Mint-green PTEN sweeps across the gold PIP3 patch, stripping 3-phosphates so gold tiles revert to slate-blue PIP2. Coral-red Akt detaches into the cytosol, sheds its two 'P' badges, and folds back to muted coral. To the left, a feedback arc adds amber-grey 'Ser-P' tags onto teal IRS-1, dimming its phosphotyrosine docking sites. Empathy fix: Show 'Ser-P' badges on IRS-1 with a PI 3-kinase failing to dock ('Ser-P IRS-1 ✕ PI3K').

scenes.tts: Test the pattern on one target. Suppose A S one sixty is mutated so Akt can no longer phosphorylate it. When insulin arrives, what happens to glucose uptake in a fat cell?
scenes.caption: Test the pattern on one target. Suppose AS160 is mutated so Akt can no longer phosphorylate it. When insulin arrives, what happens to glucose uptake in a fat cell?
scenes.visual: Return to the 'Muscle & fat' zone (schematic). Indigo AS160 carries an X over its phosphorylation site ('AS160 mutant'), still tethering emerald GLUT4 vesicles. Coral-red Akt is active on gold PIP3 above. Question card overlays the lower frame: 'Akt cannot mark AS160: what happens to glucose uptake?'.
scenes.narration: Test the pattern on one target. Suppose AS160 is mutated so Akt can no longer phosphorylate it. When insulin arrives, what happens to glucose uptake in a fat cell?

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause: question card remains visible while the X-marked AS160 holds the emerald GLUT4 vesicles and active coral-red Akt glows on the membrane above.

scenes.tts: Fewer vesicles reach the surface, so uptake rises much less, though Akt itself is active. Now push the whole relay both ways. Lose the eraser P ten, or mutate P I three kinase, and growth signals lock on in tumours. Overdo serine feedback, and insulin resistance weakens the same relay.
scenes.caption: Fewer vesicles reach the surface, so uptake rises much less, though Akt itself is active. Now push the whole relay both ways. Lose the eraser PTEN, or mutate PI 3-kinase, and growth signals lock on in tumours. Overdo serine feedback, and insulin resistance weakens the same relay.
scenes.visual: First, most emerald GLUT4 vesicles stay inside behind the X-marked AS160, with only a few fusing; label 'Uptake rises less'. Then split the membrane cross-section into two contrasting halves (schematic). Left half labelled 'Stuck on (cancer)': 'PTEN lost / PIK3CA mutant', abundant gold PIP3 and bright coral-red Akt. Right half labelled 'Turned down (insulin resistance)': teal IRS-1 with 'Ser-P' tags, dim sky-blue PI 3-kinase, sparse PIP3, and mostly muted coral Akt in the cytosol. Empathy fix: After the answer, the line 'push the whole relay both ways' introduces the two-panel 'Stuck on / Weak' split. Side notes stay on screen only: 'Growth factors: survival, growth' and 'Excess nutrients, inflammation → more serine feedback'.
scenes.narration: Fewer vesicles reach the surface, so uptake rises much less, though Akt itself is active. Now push the whole relay both ways. Lose the eraser PTEN, or mutate PI 3-kinase, and growth signals lock on in tumours. Overdo serine feedback, and insulin resistance weakens the same relay.

scenes.tts: One kinase directs muscle, fat, liver, and growing cells because each tissue supplies its own targets. Lose an eraser and the signal locks on. Overdrive feedback and the cell responds weakly to insulin. Healthy signaling pairs active Akt with reliable erasers and negative feedback.

Overdrive feedback and the cell responds weakly to insulin. Healthy signaling pairs active Akt with reliable erasers and negative feedback.
